$comment: Compliance calendar — obligation extraction across the package (spec §4.2). Immediate Deadlines are dated from formation; Recurring Obligations repeat annually or biennially. Every date shown is computed from the effective date rather than written into the text.

clauses.title: 83(b) Filing Deadline
clauses.rationale: Shortest and least forgiving deadline in the package, which is why it is listed first.
clauses.body: The [[Section 83(b) election|section 83(b) election]] must be postmarked to the IRS within 30 days of grant — that is {{d83bDeadline}} for this Company. There is no cure for a late filing. Filing instructions are in <<xr:b83_instructions>>.

clauses.title: Foreign Qualification
clauses.rationale: The obligation attaches when the company begins transacting business in the state, which is usually before anyone thinks to check.
clauses.body: The Company is formed in {{formStateLong}} but operates in {{opStateLong}}, which generally requires [[foreign qualification]] there before transacting business. Penalties typically include back fees and loss of access to that state’s courts until the Company registers. The application is in <<xr:fq_statement>>.

clauses.title: EIN and Tax Registration
clauses.rationale: Everything downstream — bank account, payroll, merchant processing — waits on the EIN.
clauses.body: An employer needs an EIN, applied for on IRS Form SS-4, before opening the bank account authorized in <<xr:consent_bank>>. Then register for {{opStateLong}} state tax accounts and, if hiring, unemployment insurance and workers’ compensation.

clauses.title: Annual Report and Registered Agent
clauses.rationale: Falling out of good standing blocks financings, bank changes, and qualification in other states, and is discovered at the worst possible moment.
clauses.body: {{formStateLong}} filing schedule: {{annualReportRule}}. Maintain the registered agent named in <<xr:charter_agent>> continuously — a lapsed agent is the most common cause of a missed filing, because that is where the state sends the notice.

clauses.title: Payroll Tax Deposits and Filings
clauses.rationale: Unremitted payroll trust fund taxes are personally recoverable from responsible individuals. This is one of the few company liabilities that pierces the entity by statute.
clauses.body: Once the Company has employees it must deposit withheld income and FICA taxes on the schedule the IRS assigns, file Form 941 quarterly and Form 940 annually, and meet the equivalent {{opStateLong}} obligations. Unremitted trust fund taxes can be assessed personally against the officer appointed in <<xr:consent_officers>>.

clauses.title: Annual BAA and Security Review
clauses.rationale: The HIPAA Security Rule requires a periodic risk analysis, and the vendor inventory drifts as vendors are added informally.
clauses.body: Covered entities commonly review the business associate inventory annually and confirm each agreement is current; the HIPAA Security Rule requires the security risk analysis. Document both — the analysis is the first thing requested after any reported incident.
